narrative.weekly_mirror: You scrubbed the indigo from your hands after Mummyji’s pointed look at lunch, and later smiled and nodded when Arjun’s teacher worried about his choice to draw instead of play cricket. “I scrubbed the indigo off after lunch.” Both moments seem to carry the weight of fitting someone else’s expectations, even as your own choices—or Arjun’s—were present underneath.
narrative.tension_explanation: Across these two moments, you moved away from choosing your own path: hiding the indigo after the lunch exchange and reassuring the teacher rather than naming that Arjun may simply prefer drawing. The pull to honour familiar expectations seems close by, but what you wanted for yourself and for Arjun remains less visible in what you said or did.
narrative.reflective_question: When you think about the lunch with Mummyji or the meeting about Arjun, which moment most made you set aside what you really wanted to say?
